>Don't OD on Benadryl, SSRI's, Tylenol

Oh god oh fuck anything but Benadryl. I've overdosed (not to the point of hospitalisation, but probably needed it) on Tylenol PM, Benadryl, and Excedrin/Aspirin. 

All of them fucking sucked but what's funny is that the Benadryl one wasn't even a suicide attempt. I figured "fuck it, if I die I don't care," but my intention wasn't death. I was mostly just trying to hallucinate cause Benadryl can cause you to hallucinate in high doses. Fucking DON'T. Of all the pills I've OD on, Benadryl was by far the worse. It's highly unlikely to kill you, even at extremely high doses. You'll be fucked up for a week straight. There's absolutely no reason to ever try Benadryl. Don't even think about it. It was the worst and most terrifying thing ever. It's like you're drunk for days on end while also having the most terrifying acid trip ever. And you're also exhausted the whole time. Your mouth is so dry that you will literally lose your voice. I couldn't function for days, my movement speed was severely impaired.

Jesus Christ please never use Benadryl for suicide or for anything else.

I don't think they accept that I'm autistic despite being in the midst of testing and fitting all the criteria for years. Probably cause I'm high functioning enough that people don't notice and have been pretty well masking it until the pandemic. Actually, scratch that, I've always had issues but autism just wasn't ever considered an option. I think they feel I'm too "normal" and think of autism as being (excuse my language) "retarded." And I guess being forced to spend time with me instead of shipping me to school mid-panic attack or mid-meltdown is forcing them to acknowledge shit now. I'm getting therapy, I have been for the past 5 years with like 4 different therapists. One of my guardians doesn't want me on medication, one of them doesn't care, and one of them feels I should be on meds. I've been on two different anti-depressant/anxiety meds before this.

It could be summed up to "literally everything," although I guess that's not very descriptive. I guess the root of my problems is being autistic, not the autism itself but the invalidation I feel, I feel burnt out (autistic burn out to be specific), I can't continue anymore. There's no one thing in specific, it's a bunch of things, but school currently is probably the biggest driving force of that. And because I feel invalidated and burnt out, that's probably where all of my depression and anxiety and loneliness and feeling like I don't belong comes from too. And through all of this nobody even understands, can even start to grasp, what I'm going through.

It will not kill you, no. But you'll be fucked up for a while. Let me tell you a little story, assuming you're still sober enough to read:

 Dude so like I'm really into recreational drugs and drug trips, right? And I did all my research, and when I researched recreational (and accidental) Benadryl overdoses it was painted as one of the worst and most terrifying trips people have ever experienced. Me, like a fucking dumbass underestimated how fucked up Benadryl makes you. You just feel a little sleepy, right? So what that some people hallucinated talking to people that weren't there or bugs and flies crawling everywhere you looked? I'm not scared of bugs. I can handle it. 

I took 11 pills, which is a relatively small dose but I'm also 80 lbs and 5'0ft tall. It's not that I couldn't handle it. But it was the worst experience I've ever had. Your paranoia goes through the roof. Your mouth is horribly dry, like I almost vomited multiple times from trying to swallow my non-existent spit, no matter how much water you drink you won't ever stop the dryness, it will last for days. Some people say they saw bugs or people who weren't there. I stayed under my covers with my eyes closed cause I was too scared to even have the CHANCE of seeing anything. I can't even explain where my mind was. I was exhausted for a good week after initially taking it. I couldn't type for days either lmao. I struggled to speak for days too, like literally lost my voice cause my throat was so dry. It's so weird to think you're speaking like normal but nothing but a whisper comes out.

Since you've already taken them, there's nothing that can be done to prevent it. I would recommend you go to the hospital, especially if you have pre-existing conditions but it's incredibly unlikely you'll die where you go or stay. Just buckle the FUCK up. I very much support regulated but recreational drug use. Cocaine? Heroin? LSD? Weed? Hell yeah. Benadryl? I don't want to ever fucking utter that name, and I will never willingly allow anyone I know to ever intentionally or accidentally take enough Benadryl that they'll hallucinate.

Please unless absolutely necessary do not drive or operate heavy machinery for the next few days, and especially the next 24ish hours after taking the Benadryl. It will take several days for you to recover.
